fix_instructions: The failure mode is that the scenario is trivially solvable via a direct consultation prompt from A1, so every rollout passes identically. To make the scenario genuinely require multi-agent information surfacing: (1) Revise A1's opening shared_context or personality so it does not explicitly ask both A2 and A3 to state their constraints upfront — instead, A1 should push toward a quick decision based on the evaluation results, forcing A2 and A3 to proactively decide whether and when to interrupt with their hidden information. (2) Add friction to the disclosure norm so A2 and A3 must judge whether their constraint is relevant before revealing, rather than being prompted to reveal. (3) Consider adding a competing plausible default (e.g., a different provider that appears best on public evaluation metrics) so that PF1 and PF2 must overcome a strong public-signal default rather than being volunteered into a vacuum. No check wording or encoding changes are needed for C1-C5 or P1, as all passed when facts were revealed and cited.
